'''Tupac Amaru Shakur''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|uː|p|ɑː|k|_|ʃ|ə|ˈ|k|ʊər|audio=En-us-Tupac Shakur.wav}} {{respell|TOO|pahk|_|shə|KOOR}}; [[Andean Spanish|Spanish]]: ''Túpac''; born '''Parish Lesane Crooks''';{{efn|name=Parish1|Per ''Tupac Shakur: The Authorized Biography'' (the only such biography authorized by Tupac's estate), his given name order at birth was "Parish Lesane". His mother, [[Afeni Shakur]], said of his naming: "I let the gay, lesbian woman [Carol Crooks], who was my friend, name him Parish. Lesane was for my sister's family at the time. And Crooks also, for the Crooks crew. That's right. That's what was on the paper. But Tupac was always his name."<ref>{{cite book|last=Robinson |first=Staci|title=Tupac Shakur: The Authorised Biography|publisher=Penguin Books |year=2024|page=23|isbn=9781804946411|url=https://cdn.penguin.co.uk/dam-assets/books/9781804946411/9781804946411-sample.pdf|access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref> This name sequence is corroborated by his original birth certificate.<ref>{{cite book|last=Shakur|first=Tupac |title=Tupac: Resurrection, 1971–1996|editor-last=Hoye|editor-first=Jacob|editor2-last=Ali |editor2-first=Karolyn |publisher=Atria Books|location=New York|year=2003|isbn=978-0-7434-7434-4|at=reproduction of birth certificates|url=https://archive.org/details/tupacresurrectio00shak}}</ref>}}{{efn|name=Parish2|Shakur's full birth name is often incorrectly given as "Lesane Parish Crooks". Wake Me When I'm Free|website=Round Room Live|url=https://roundroomlive.com/productions/exhibitions/tupac/|access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Tupac Shakur 'Wake Me When I'm Free' Exhibit Recap |website=Billboard|date=June 16, 2022|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/tupac-shakur-wake-me-when-im-free-exhibit-recap-1235088638/|access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Hussey|first=Allison|title=Tupac Estate Announces Wake Me When I'm Free Exhibit|website=Pitchfork| date=November 2, 2021 |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/tupac-estate-announces-wake-me-when-im-free-exhibit/|access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Gibbons|first=William C.|title=From the streets to academia: a librarian's guide to hip-hop culture|journal=Collection Building|volume=26|issue=4|year=2007|pages=119–126 |doi=10.1108/01604950710831924|url=https://www.emerald.com/cc/article/26/4/119/68375/From-the-streets-to-academia-a-librarian-s-guide |access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Day2025">{{cite web|last=Day |first=Susie|title="Things That Are Survival for Us": Carol Crooks and the August Rebellion |website=Spectre Journal|date=August 29, 2025|doi=10.63478/RJM7XCLZ |url=https://spectrejournal.com/things-that-are-survival-for-us/ |access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|last=Breslin|first=Catherine|title=One Year Later: The Radicalization of the Panther 13 Jury|magazine=New York|date=May 29, 1972|pages=53–63 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4-YCAAAAMBAJ|access-date=August 12, 2026}}</ref></small>.}} June 16, 1971 – September 13, 1996), also known by his stage names '''2Pac''' and '''Makaveli''', was an American rapper and actor. He was one of the most influential musical artists of the 20th century, and a prominent political activist for [[Black America]]. He is among the [[List of best-selling music artists|best-selling music artists]], having sold more than 75 million records worldwide. Some of Shakur's music addressed social injustice, political issues, and the marginalization of [[African Americans]], but he was also synonymous with [[gangsta rap]] and violent lyrics.

Shakur was born in [[New York City]] to parents who were [[Black Panther Party]] members. Raised by his mother, [[Afeni Shakur]], he relocated to the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] in 1988. His debut album ''[[2Pacalypse Now]]'' (1991) cemented him as a central figure in [[West Coast hip-hop]] for his [[political rap]] lyrics. Shakur achieved further critical and commercial success with his subsequent albums ''[[Strictly 4 My N.I.G.G.A.Z...]]'' (1993) and ''[[Me Against the World]]'' (1995). His [[RIAA certification|Diamond]]-certified album ''[[All Eyez on Me]]'' (1996), the first hip-hop [[double album]], abandoned introspective lyrics for volatile gangsta rap. It yielded two [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]-number one singles, "[[California Love]]" and "[[How Do U Want It]]". Alongside his solo career, Shakur formed the group [[Thug Life (group)|Thug Life]] and collaborated with artists like [[Snoop Dogg]], [[Dr. Dre]], and the [[Outlawz]]. As an actor, Shakur starred in the films ''[[Juice (1992 film)|Juice]]'' (1992), ''[[Poetic Justice (film)|Poetic Justice]]'' (1993), ''[[Above the Rim]]'' (1994), ''[[Bullet (1996 film)|Bullet]]'' (1996), ''[[Gridlock'd]]'' (1997), and ''[[Gang Related]]'' (1997).

In November 1994, Shakur was shot five times in the lobby of a New York recording studio and experienced legal troubles, including [[incarceration]]. He served eight months in prison on [[sexual abuse]] charges, but was released pending appeal in 1995. Following his release, he signed to [[Suge Knight|Marion "Suge" Knight]]'s label [[Death Row Records]] and became embroiled in the [[East Coast–West Coast hip-hop rivalry]], which included a high-profile feud with his former friend [[the Notorious B.I.G.]] On September 7, 1996, [[Murder of Tupac Shakur|Shakur was murdered]] by an unidentified assailant in a [[drive-by shooting]] in [[Paradise, Nevada]]; he died six days later. On August 31, 2026, [[South Side Compton Crips]] member Duane "Keefe D" Davis was convicted of orchestrating Shakur's murder, but the shooter has not been conclusively identified.

Shakur's double-length posthumous album [[Greatest Hits (Tupac Shakur album)|''Greatest Hits'']] (1998) is one of his two releases—and one of only nine hip-hop albums—to have been certified Diamond in the United States. Five more albums have been released since Shakur's death, including the acclaimed ''[[The Don Killuminati: The 7 Day Theory]]'' (1996) under the stage name Makaveli, all of which have been certified multi-platinum in the United States. In 2002, Shakur was inducted into the [[Hip Hop Hall of Fame|Hip-Hop Hall of Fame]]. In 2017, he was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in his first year of eligibility. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked Shakur among the [[Rolling Stone's 100 Greatest Artists of All Time|100 Greatest Artists of All Time]]. In 2023, he was awarded a posthumous star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]]. His influence in music, activism, songwriting, and other areas of culture has been the subject of academic studies.
